A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIRECTO study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-generation experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, architectural ablations, and dataset-size and sampling studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds label-sensitive evaluation, model-capacity and graph-size experiments, and conditional TPU generation results. Table 21 separately attributes its baseline scores to prior work.

M1.justification: v2 adds classifier-free guidance for execution-time-conditioned TPU graph generation (Section 5.1 and Appendix H.7). This extends the generation procedure while retaining the original dual-attention architecture, positional encodings, and unconditional flow-matching and diffusion algorithms.

E1.justification: Coverage expands beyond unconditional generation to execution-time-conditioned TPU generation. Appendix H.6 also adds ER-DAG populations with 80–150, 150–200, and 200–250 nodes, extending the earlier 20–80-node coverage. These introduce a distinct task requirement and substantially larger input structures; the original dataset families remain.

E2.justification: The new conditional comparison in Table 21 adds GraphRNN, GraphPNAS, OneShotDAG, and LayerDAG (T=1), alongside D-VAE and LayerDAG. These are reported comparators using scores explicitly obtained from Li et al. (2025), rather than newly reproduced baselines. The original unconditional comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces node-type MMD, semantic-tuple precision/recall, embedding-based FID and RBF MMD, and surrogate-based conditional evaluation. It adds larger-model and larger-graph protocols and revises sampling settings for retained experiments: for example, Table 7 changes SBM RRWP's omega from 0.01 to 0.1 and eta from 10 to 50. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New comparisons with larger non-dual networks test whether model capacity explains dual attention's gains (Tables 2 and 18). Graph-size experiments test runtime, fidelity, and acyclicity at scale (Tables 19–20), while Figures 4–5 revise sampling-sensitivity evidence. The earlier dual-attention, positional-encoding, and tenfold dataset-size studies are retained under new numbering.

E5.justification: Table 21 introduces averaging over three runs for conditional generation, with variability reported alongside the averages. Retained main experiments continue reporting means and standard deviations over five sampling runs, and the single-run TPU sampling-search exception remains.

E6.justification: v2 adds label-sensitive, capacity, graph-size, and conditional results, including only 2.0% validity for 200–250-node ER-DAGs. Existing scores and sampling curves also change: SBM DIRECTO-RRWP V.U.N. changes from 87.0% to 99.5% under revised sampling settings, so this is not a same-setting gain. DeFoG's Visual Genome V.U.N. is unresolved within v2: Table 1 reports 50.8%, whereas Table 10 retains 39.6%.

T1.justification: Appendix H.6 adds a computational-complexity claim that dual attention introduces at most a constant factor of two overhead while preserving standard graph-transformer asymptotic complexity. No proof accompanies this addition. The existing attention, positional-encoding, and flow/diffusion derivations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions—directed flow matching, directional architectural components, and a benchmarking framework—remain. v2 adds an explicit main-text claim that the framework extends readily to conditional generation through classifier-free guidance; the earlier broad performance and novelty claims largely persist.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the brief Appendix K discussion with specific limitations concerning scalability, conditioning, structural constraints, downstream applicability, and interpretability. Appendix H newly discusses partial memorization, interprets capacity comparisons as evidence for directional inductive bias, and explains the difficulty of preserving acyclicity in larger graphs. Conditional-generation discussion also qualifies the suitability of its guidance strategy and evaluation.

D1.justification: v2 documents the conditional-guidance search grid and selected strength of 0.25, clarifies that retained architectural ablations optimize time distortion but not omega or eta, and explicitly identifies Q=1 in dual-attention ablations. These disclosures do not establish changed underlying ablation procedures. The code-access footnote changes from the named GitHub repository to an anonymous repository.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references for conditional guidance, graph and scene-graph metrics, and scalable or constrained generation. It also replaces the DDIM background citation with score-based diffusion references. The central positioning relative to undirected generators and Law et al.'s directed autoregressive work remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten and reorganized. Section 3.2 condenses positional-encoding explanations whose details remain in Appendix B; the denoising background is reordered; separate ablation subsections are merged; and Appendices H and K are substantially reorganized. Citation style and heading conventions also change throughout.

P2.justification: The two detailed main benchmark tables become appendix Tables 9–10, while a new cross-dataset summary occupies Table 1. New displays cover label-sensitive metrics, capacity, graph size, and conditional generation. Sampling plots are redrawn with changed curves and axis ranges, and the document adopts a different layout template. Figures 1–3 and most graph visualizations are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: The added label-sensitive evaluation and capacity tests address gaps in assessing semantic fidelity and architectural benefits, while larger-graph failures and conditional results clarify applicability beyond v1. These gains are tempered by conflicting DeFoG scores in Tables 1 and 10, an incorrect node-type MMD interpretation around Table 11, and inconsistent descriptions of the capacity control as widening versus doubling depth. The net improvement is therefore limited.
